Density bundle (∣ΛnT∗M∣)

Words: 79 Articles: 1
Vector bundle OurBigBook.com
On an n-dimensional smooth manifold, the density bundle ∣ΛnT∗M∣ is the real line bundle whose coordinate transformation uses the absolute value of the Jacobian determinant. A density can therefore be integrated without an orientation of a smooth manifold. A Riemannian metric gives the positive density det(gij​)​∣dx1⋯dxn∣, including on a nonorientable manifold.
// Target: fiber-bundle.bigb

Riemannian volume density (dμg​)

Words: 32
Density bundle OurBigBook.com
A Riemannian metric on a smooth manifold gives a positive section of the density bundle, locally dμg​=det(gij​)​∣dx1⋯dxn∣. The absolute Jacobian determinant makes this independent of coordinates without requiring orientability. With an orientation of a smooth manifold, it corresponds to the Riemannian volume form.

Tensor bundle (Tsr​M)

Words: 42
Vector bundle OurBigBook.com
For a smooth manifold M, the tensor bundle Tsr​M=(TM)⊗r⊗(T∗M)⊗s is a vector bundle whose smooth sections of a vector bundle are tensor fields of type (r,s). Its transition functions of a vector bundle are tensor products of the tangent bundle transition matrices and their inverse transposes. Symmetric tensors and differential forms arise from the symmetric and alternating subbundles.
// Target: fiber-bundle.bigb

G-structure on a vector bundle (P⊆Fr(E),G⊆GL(m,R))

Words: 56
Vector bundle OurBigBook.com
A G-structure on a real rank-m vector bundle is a principal G reduction of its frame bundle. Equivalently it has local frames whose transition matrices take values in G, with the reduction consisting of their right G-orbits. An orthogonal structure on a real vector bundle is equivalent to a fiber metric; a special orthogonal reduction is equivalent to that metric together with an orientation of a vector bundle.

Globally generated vector bundle (H0(C,F)⊗OC​↠F)

Words: 181 Articles: 2
Vector bundle OurBigBook.com
A vector bundle is globally generated when its global sections span every fibre. The evaluation map in the display expresses this condition. On a projective curve its space of global sections is finite-dimensional, so a finite collection of sections suffices.

Global generation of positive twists on a smooth curve (E⊗OC​(mp0​) is globally generated for m≫0)

Words: 70
Globally generated vector bundle OurBigBook.com
For a vector bundle of finite positive rank let B be an upper degree bound for the line subbundles of E∗⊗KC​. If m−1>B, no nonzero map OC​(mp0​−p)→E∗⊗KC​ can exist for any point p: its saturated image would have degree at least m−1. Serre duality then gives H1(E(mp0​−p))=0. The evaluation exact sequence shows that H0(E(mp0​))→E(mp0​)∣p​ is surjective at every point, proving the assertion with a uniform bound in p.

Nowhere-vanishing section of a globally generated bundle on a curve

Words: 77
Globally generated vector bundle OurBigBook.com
Let F be globally generated of rank r≥2 on a projective curve, and put W=H0(C,F). The pairs (p,s) with s(p)=0 form the total space of the kernel of the evaluation map over the curve. This incidence variety has dimension dimW+1−r<dimW. Its image in W is closed because the curve is proper, and is a proper subset by the dimension bound. A section outside it vanishes nowhere and gives a line subbundle OC​⊂F with locally free quotient.

Whitney sum of vector bundles ((E⊕F)x​=Ex​⊕Fx​)

Words: 37
Vector bundle OurBigBook.com
The fiberwise direct sum of two vector bundles over the same base. It is formed from the fiber product of their total spaces, with the direct-sum linear structure in each fiber. Transition matrices are block diagonal.
// Target: geometry-and-topology.bigb

Symplectic vector bundle

Words: 77 Articles: 1
Vector bundle OurBigBook.com
A symplectic vector bundle has a smooth fiberwise symplectic form, making each fiber a symplectic vector space. Its structure group reduces to the symplectic group. A symplectic normal bundle is an important example.

Lagrangian subbundle

Words: 51
Symplectic vector bundle OurBigBook.com
A rank-n vector subbundle of a rank-2n symplectic vector bundle is Lagrangian when each fibre is a Lagrangian subspace. If it exists, a compatible almost complex structure supplies a complementary Lagrangian subbundle by applying J. Existence is a global condition: the area-oriented tangent bundle of the two-sphere has no real line subbundle, by triviality of real line bundles over the sphere and the Hairy ball theorem.

Thom space (Th(ξ)=D(ξ)/S(ξ))

Words: 127 Articles: 1
Vector bundle OurBigBook.com
For a real vector bundle over a compact base, its Thom space is the quotient of its disk bundle by its sphere bundle, with the collapsed sphere bundle as basepoint. Equivalently it is the one-point compactification of the total space. An oriented bundle's Thom class and Thom isomorphism identify the reduced cohomology of this space with shifted cohomology of the base.

Projective-space quotient as a Thom space of conjugate tautological lines (CPn+m+1/CPn≅Th(γˉ​⊕(n+1)→CPm))

Words: 71
Thom space OurBigBook.com
Decompose the ambient vector space as V⊕W, of dimensions n+1,m+1. A projective line outside P(V) is the graph of a unique linear map from a line in W to V. Thus the complement is the total space of γ∗⊗V, which is complex-isomorphic to γˉ​⊕(n+1) after choosing a Hermitian metric. Collapsing P(V) gives its one-point compactification, hence the Thom space because the base is compact.
// Target: geometry-and-topology.bigb

Line subbundle

Words: 32
Vector bundle OurBigBook.com
A line subbundle is an injective map from a line bundle into a vector bundle whose quotient is locally free. Equivalently the injection splits locally. On a smooth algebraic curve, saturation of a rank-one coherent subsheaf produces a saturated line subbundle on a smooth curve.

Birkhoff–Grothendieck theorem (E≅⨁i​O(ai​))

Words: 79
Vector bundle OurBigBook.com
Every vector bundle on the projective line over a field splits as a direct sum of line bundles. Choose the largest integer a with H0(E(−a))=0. A corresponding map O(a)→E is saturated, since saturation otherwise increases its degree. Inductively split its quotient as ⨁i​O(bi​). Twisting the exact sequence by −a−1 and using H1(O(−1))=0 gives bi​≤a. Hence all extension groups H1(O(a−bi​)) vanish, and the sequence splits. The multiset of degrees is determined by the dimensions of all twisted global-section spaces.

Stable framing of a vector bundle

Words: 54
Vector bundle OurBigBook.com
A framing is a continuous ordered basis in every fiber, equivalently a trivialization of the vector bundle. A stable framing trivializes the bundle after adding trivial real summands, up to further stabilization and homotopy. For a smooth map it is the stable normal data that is framed, not necessarily the tangent bundle of either manifold.

Endomorphism bundle (EndE=E⊗E∗)

Words: 52
Vector bundle OurBigBook.com
The vector bundle whose fibre at p consists of linear maps Ep​→Ep​. If a local frame changes by e′=eg, the coefficient matrix of an endomorphism changes by T′=g−1Tg, giving smooth fibre-linear transitions. For a line bundle this bundle is canonically the trivial scalar bundle, because every fibre endomorphism is scalar multiplication. A connection on a vector bundle induces the endomorphism bundle connection.

Exterior power of a vector bundle (ΛrE)

Words: 60
Vector bundle OurBigBook.com
For a rank-k smooth vector bundle, take the exterior power ΛrEp​ in each fibre. A local frame gives a trivialization with fibre ΛrRk, and a transition matrix A acts by ΛrA. Functoriality preserves the cocycle identities, producing a smooth vector bundle of rank (rk​), or the zero bundle when r>k. Its top exterior power is the determinant line bundle.

Clutching construction

Words: 185 Articles: 2
Vector bundle OurBigBook.com
A vector bundle over Sn can be constructed by gluing two trivial bundles over its hemispheres with a transition map γ:Sn−1→GL(k,R). Extend this map constantly in an equatorial collar to obtain local vector bundle trivializations. A transition map into the special orthogonal group gives compatible fiber orientations and a fiber metric. Homotopies of transition maps give isomorphic bundles.

Clutching function (γ:Sn−1→SO(k))

Words: 133 Articles: 1
Clutching construction OurBigBook.com
A clutching function is the equatorial transition map used in the clutching construction. For an oriented real vector bundle one may choose a fiber metric and orthonormal trivializations, so its clutching function takes values in the special orthogonal group.

Section obstruction for a clutched vector bundle ([u↦γ(u)ek​]∈πn−1​(Sk−1))

Words: 101
Clutching function OurBigBook.com
For an oriented rank-k bundle over Sn, with k≥2, normalize its clutching function to be based at the identity. A nowhere-zero section exists precisely when the displayed homotopy class vanishes. If it vanishes, extend γek​ across one hemisphere and use the constant section ek​ on the other. Conversely normalize any nowhere-zero section using the fiber metric. Its two hemisphere maps satisfy σ−​=γσ+​ on the boundary. The first hemisphere makes σ+​ homotopic to a constant; the second makes γσ+​ null-homotopic. Thus γek​ is null-homotopic. If k>n, the lower homotopy group of the sphere vanishes and a section always exists. Rank one is already trivial because SO(1) is trivial.

Clifford module bundle (c:T∗M→End(E))

Words: 47
Vector bundle OurBigBook.com
A Clifford module bundle is a vector bundle over a Riemannian manifold with a fibrewise Clifford multiplication. A compatible connection on a vector bundle satisfies [∇X​,c(α)]=c(∇X​α) for the Levi-Civita connection on covectors. On a graded Clifford module bundle, Clifford multiplication exchanges the two grading summands. The associated Dirac operator is D=∑i​c(ei)∇ei​​. Its fibres are modules over the fibres of the Clifford algebra bundle.

Determinant line bundle (detE=⋀rankEE)

Words: 49
Vector bundle OurBigBook.com
The top exterior power of a rank-r vector bundle is its determinant line bundle. A short exact sequence of vector bundles gives a canonical isomorphism of the middle determinant with the tensor product of the other two. Locally, a subbundle frame followed by lifts of a quotient frame defines it; changing lifts only adds off-diagonal blocks. This is the determinant step in adjunction for a smooth submanifold.

Zero section of a vector bundle (0E​:X→E)

Words: 35
Vector bundle OurBigBook.com
The zero section sends each base point to the zero vector in its fiber. It is a smooth section of a vector bundle and an embedded copy of the base. The Liouville one-form vanishes as an ambient covector precisely along the zero section of a cotangent bundle.

Fiber metric (hx​:Ex​×Ex​→R)

Words: 198 Articles: 3
Vector bundle OurBigBook.com
A fiber metric on a real smooth vector bundle is a positive-definite inner product on each fiber that varies smoothly in vector bundle trivializations. A smooth partition of unity subordinate to trivializing charts averages their Euclidean inner products. Nonnegative weights preserve positivity and local finiteness ensures smoothness. Hence every real vector bundle over a Hausdorff second-countable smooth manifold admits a fiber metric. Applied to the tangent bundle, this is existence of a Riemannian metric.

Orthogonal structure on a real vector bundle (O(r))

Words: 137 Articles: 2
Fiber metric OurBigBook.com
An orthogonal structure is a reduction of the transition functions of a real rank-r vector bundle to the orthogonal group. Its orthonormal frames define a fiber metric, independent of the chosen frame because orthogonal transitions preserve the inner product. Conversely a fiber metric gives smooth orthonormal frames by the Gram-Schmidt process, with orthogonal transition matrices. This equivalence does not require the vector bundle to be globally trivial.

Euclidean orthonormal frame (g(ei​,ej​)=δij​)

Words: 40
Orthogonal structure on a real vector bundle OurBigBook.com
This is a frame of a real vector bundle with a positive-definite fiber metric for which the basis vectors are orthonormal. The Gram-Schmidt process applied to any smooth local frame produces such frames smoothly. They are distinguished from Lorentzian orthonormal frames, whose metric has mixed signature.

Orthogonal local trivialization (h(ei​,ej​)=δij​)

Words: 39
Orthogonal structure on a real vector bundle OurBigBook.com
A vector bundle trivialization is orthogonal when its coordinate frame is orthonormal for the fiber metric, so each fiber is identified isometrically with Euclidean space. Overlap changes then take values in the orthogonal group. Local orthogonal trivializations exist even when no global frame does.

Eigenbundle (ker(A−λI))

Words: 37
Vector bundle OurBigBook.com
For a smooth complex vector bundle endomorphism A and a smooth eigenvalue function λ, a kernel of constant rank is a smooth vector subbundle, called its eigenbundle. Without a constant-rank hypothesis these kernels need not form a vector bundle.

Hermitian vector bundle ((E,h))

Words: 38
Vector bundle OurBigBook.com
A Hermitian vector bundle is a complex vector bundle with a smoothly varying positive definite Hermitian form on each fibre. When the bundle is holomorphic, this is a Hermitian metric on a holomorphic vector bundle. Orthogonal projection to a smooth subbundle produces its induced metric and the quotient Hermitian metric.

Complex vector bundle (E→X)

Words: 272 Articles: 4
Vector bundle OurBigBook.com
A complex vector bundle is a vector bundle with complex-linear local trivializations and transition maps. A rank-r complex bundle has an underlying oriented real bundle of rank 2r, using the orientation of complex bases. Rank-one bundles are complex line bundles, and their higher-rank counterparts have integral Chern classes.

Hermitian metric on a smooth complex vector bundle (hb​:Eb​×Eb​→C)

Words: 53
Complex vector bundle OurBigBook.com
This is a smoothly varying positive-definite Hermitian form on each fiber, without requiring a holomorphic base or bundle. A partition of unity glues local positive metrics into a global one. Applying smooth Gram-Schmidt to local frames then makes the transitions unitary, reducing the structure group of a vector bundle to U(k). For a line bundle its unit vectors form a principal bundle for the circle group.

Stable complex structure on a real vector bundle

Words: 67
Complex vector bundle OurBigBook.com
For an even-rank real vector bundle ξ, a stable complex structure is a complex structure on ξ⊕R2s, considered up to adding trivial complex bundles and homotopy.
